title: Ancient DNA Extraction from Skeletal Material
author: Irina Velsko
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.baksicwe
materials: High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid kit
Irradiate all buffers with UV for 00:30:00 without the lids. UV irradiation can be done together with solutions from steps 1 (binding buffer), 4 (wash buffer), and 5 (TET buffer).

Prepare cleaned workspace with all necessary reagents and equipment. If lab-wide large-batch pre-prepared reagent stores are used, ensure to have made personal stock-aliquot of reagents such as UV-Water, EDTA, sodium acetate, and proteinase K in amounts sufficient for this extraction.
Prepare cleaned workspace with all necessary reagents and equipment.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer
steps.instruction: Make 10 mL of binding buffer per reaction; store the bottle at 4 °C overnight, label with name, date and number of reactions, and seal with Parafilm to avoid evaporation (stable up to four weeks).

steps.title: Prepare wash buffer
steps.instruction: Add 40 mL ethanol to the wash buffer supplied in the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid kit, mix, then aliquot 900 µL per reaction; keep on ice until use.

steps.title: Prepare TET elution buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 100 µL TE‑buffer with Tween‑20 to reach a final concentration of 0.05 % (v/v); because Tween‑20 is viscous, first dilute it 1:10 in UV‑irradiated HPLC water and add the 10 % Tween‑20 solution to the TE‑buffer.

steps.title: Prepare GuHCl solution
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of GuHCl into a glass bottle, add UV‑irradiated HPLC water to the final desired volume (part of the extraction buffer), gently shake horizontally until dissolved; if needed, apply 10‑second bursts of ~400 W microwave while the bottle is slightly unscrewed, allowing cooling between bursts. The dissolution is endothermic and the tube will become very cold; handle accordingly.

steps.title: Add isopropanol to GuHCl
steps.instruction: Pipette isopropanol into the GuHCl solution until the total reaction volume reaches 10 mL.

steps.title: Prepare extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Follow the table referenced in step 8 to make a 1 mL extraction buffer per reaction; include 0.9 mL of 0.5 M EDTA (pH 8.0) that has been UV‑irradiated for 30 min, and any other components listed in the table.

steps.title: Dilute proteinase K
steps.instruction: Dissolve 100 mg proteinase K powder in 10 mL sterile water to obtain a concentration of 10 mg mL⁻¹; store the solution at –20 °C.

steps.title: Gather reaction consumables
steps.instruction: For each reaction, prepare one 50 mL Falcon tube, one High Pure Extender Assembly (Falcon tube with funnel and purification column), two collection tubes from the kit, and one 1.5 mL LoBind tube for the final elution.

steps.title: Add binding buffer and sodium acetate
steps.instruction: Into each 50 mL Falcon tube pipette 10 mL binding buffer and 400 µL UV‑irradiated sodium acetate; invert to mix, then measure pH (target 5–6). If pH is too high, add more sodium acetate; if too low, add sodium hydroxide.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer to bone powder
steps.instruction: Pipette 1 mL of the prepared extraction buffer onto 30–50 mg bone or tooth powder that has been placed in a labelled 2 mL Safe‑Lock tube (powder should be prepared beforehand in a dedicated sampling room).

steps.title: Incubate overnight
steps.instruction: Seal the tubes with Parafilm, place them in an incubator at 37 °C and rotate at a low overhead speed (12–16 rpm) for 12–18 h. After incubation, lysate and pellet may be stored at –20 °C. Begin day‑2 preparations (e.g., pre‑label Falcon tubes for the next step).

steps.title: Pellet bone powder
steps.instruction: Remove Parafilm and centrifuge the tubes for 00:02:00 at 18 500 × g, °C. If the pellet is not solid, repeat the centrifugation.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant
steps.instruction: Pipette the supernatant into a matching 50 mL Falcon tube and mix by inversion. If the pellet is fragile, repeat centrifugation before transferring. Store the bone pellet at –20 °C.

steps.title: Load column assembly
steps.instruction: Pipette the binding‑buffer/extract mixture onto the High Pure Extender Assembly (column funnel).

steps.title: Centrifuge column assembly
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the assembly at a maximum of 1500 rpm (adjust to the appropriate RCF for your rotor) for 00:08:00; after 00:04:00 turn the tube 180° to prevent liquid from sticking to the funnel rim.

steps.title: Collect remaining liquid
steps.instruction: Pipette any liquid remaining in the funnel onto the column, then remove the funnel and place the column into a fresh collection tube.

steps.title: Dry‑spin column (first)
steps.instruction: Dry‑spin the column in the collection tube for 00:02:00 at 18 500 × g, °C.

steps.title: Wash column (first)
steps.instruction: Add 450 µL wash buffer (from the High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid kit) to the column and centrifuge at 8000 × g, °C for 00:01:00.

steps.title: Wash column (second)
steps.instruction: Remove the column from the collection tube, discard the flow‑through and the used collection tube, place the column into a fresh collection tube, and repeat the 450 µL wash step once more using the same collection tube. Discard the second flow‑through by either pipetting it out or pouring it into a waste tube, then pat the tube rim dry with a single spot of paper tissue; clean the work surface with DNA‑Away or bleach afterwards.

steps.title: Dry‑spin column (final)
steps.instruction: Dry‑spin the column for 00:01:00 at 18 500 × g, °C. Optionally spin for 00:00:30, turn the tube 180°, then spin another 00:00:30 to ensure no liquid remains on the funnel rim.

steps.title: First DNA elution
steps.instruction: Transfer the column into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube, pipette 50 µL TET onto the centre of the column, incubate for 00:03:00, then centrifuge for 00:01:00 at 18 500 × g, °C. Label the tube on top and side.

steps.title: Second DNA elution
steps.instruction: Repeat the elution step with an additional 50 µL TET to achieve a total elution volume of 100 µL TET.

steps.title: Store DNA extracts
steps.instruction: Store the eluted DNA extracts at –20 °C until further use.
